title: Economist/YouGov Poll Found 36% Approved of Trump’s Job Performance in July 2026
description_short: An Economist/YouGov poll conducted July 17–20, 2026 found 36% approved and 60% disapproved of Trump’s job performance.
description_medium: The July 17–20, 2026 Economist/YouGov poll asked whether respondents approved or disapproved of the way Donald Trump was handling his job as president. Its official crosstabs report 36% approval and 60% disapproval among U.S. adult citizens. This is one dated poll result; it does not substantiate the separate New York Times average or CNN/SSRS Iran-war figure in the original composite title.
description_long: An Economist/YouGov poll conducted July 17–20, 2026 asked respondents: “Do you approve or disapprove of the way Donald Trump is handling his job as President?” The poll’s official crosstabs identify a sample of 1,602 U.S. adult citizens. They report 36% approval, 60% disapproval, and 4% not sure; 18% strongly approved and 17% somewhat approved. The same tables show 11% somewhat disapproved and 50% strongly disapproved. YouGov’s published summary reports the 36% approval and 60% disapproval totals. These figures support a narrow, dated account of one survey’s overall presidential job-approval measure. They do not validate the original composite claim’s 38% New York Times polling average or its separate 74% CNN/SSRS result about the Iran war’s cost. Those are different sources and measures, and the packet does not supply the CNN/SSRS poll link or question text. Do not combine the results into one poll or imply that this July survey measured views about the Iran war. The survey reports public responses at that time; it does not establish the reasons behind them or demonstrate a policy effect.
